CHEAP_DATA_NOW: Official DGCL section 262 and SEC merger documents are free; a small holder cannot cheaply guarantee an economically viable court proceeding.
CHEAP_EXPRESSION: One hypothetical standalone small-holder appraisal election, subject to all standing/notice/holding rules. No price or litigation-outcome comparison.
ECONOMIC_SIGNIFICANCE: No cheap autonomous standalone small-account expression demonstrated.
FAILED_CRITERIA: Cheap enforceable small-holder route independent of other petitioners/counsel.
FATAL_PROBLEM: For exchange-listed shares the court dismisses unless total eligible shares exceed 1%, total merger consideration exceeds $1m, or a listed short-form exception applies. Thresholds are collective, not individual: piggybacking may exist but is not an independently enforceable small-account route. Legal/funding costs and adverse fair-value risk dominate a cheap standalone experiment.
LESSON: Read standing thresholds as collective; statutory interest alone does not establish a capturable rent.
MECHANISM: A qualifying merger dissenter can seek judicial fair value plus statutory interest instead of accepting merger consideration.
NEXT_DECISION: L0 exchange-listed baby-bond full-call notices: verify fixed redemption entitlement and public exact clock without prices.
POWER_LIMITATION: Legal filter only; no economic sample.
UNCERTAINTY: Aggregation, contingent-fee counsel and exception cases are not ruled out; no blanket rejection of appraisal.
WHO_PAYS: Surviving entity if court-awarded fair value/interest exceeds the contractual merger payment.
WHY_PERSIST: Procedural burden, litigation cost, delayed capital return, uncertain valuation and collective-standing thresholds.
documentary_facts: DGCL 262(g): listed-share de minimis threshold >1% or >$1m collectively, with sections 253/267 exception.
DGCL 262(h): default interest 5% above discount rate, subject to statute/court; interest is not riskless alpha.
